description: NaCa₃Fe₃Al(SiO₃)₈ is Esseneite-derived structured and crystallizes in the monoclinic P2 space group. Na is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.39-2.79 Å. There are three inequivalent Ca sites. In the first Ca site, Ca is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Ca-O bond distances ranging from 2.35-2.85 Å. In the second Ca site, Ca is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Ca-O bond distances ranging from 2.31-2.76 Å. In the third Ca site, Ca is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Ca-O bond distances ranging from 2.35-2.79 Å. There are three inequivalent Fe sites. In the first Fe site, Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with six SiO₄ tetrahedra and edges with two equivalent FeO₆ octahedra. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 2.09-2.18 Å. In the second Fe site, Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with six SiO₄ tetrahedra and edges with two equivalent AlO₆ octahedra. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 2.08-2.18 Å. In the third Fe site, Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with six SiO₄ tetrahedra and edges with two equivalent FeO₆ octahedra. There are four shorter (2.14 Å) and two longer (2.22 Å) Fe-O bond lengths. Al is bonded to six O atoms to form AlO₆ octahedra that share corners with six SiO₄ tetrahedra and edges with two equivalent FeO₆ octahedra. There are a spread of Al-O bond distances ranging from 1.89-2.04 Å. There are four inequivalent Si sites. In the first Si site, Si is bonded to four O atoms to form SiO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one AlO₆ octahedra, corners with two FeO₆ octahedra, and corners with two equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 38-62°. There are a spread of Si-O bond distances ranging from 1.60-1.70 Å. In the second Si site, Si is bonded to four O atoms to form SiO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with three FeO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 34-59°. There are a spread of Si-O bond distances ranging from 1.61-1.69 Å. In the third Si site, Si is bonded to four O atoms to form SiO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one AlO₆ octahedra, corners with two FeO₆ octahedra, and corners with two equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 35-64°. There are a spread of Si-O bond distances ranging from 1.61-1.70 Å. In the fourth Si site, Si is bonded to four O atoms to form SiO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one AlO₆ octahedra, corners with two FeO₆ octahedra, and corners with two equivalent SiO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 33-59°. There are a spread of Si-O bond distances ranging from 1.61-1.69 Å. There are twelve inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted T-shaped geometry to one Ca, one Fe, and one Si atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted T-shaped geometry to one Ca, one Fe, and one Si atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted T-shaped geometry to one Ca, one Fe, and one Si atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted T-shaped geometry to one Na, one Al, and one Si atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to two Ca and two Si atoms. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ca, and two Si atoms. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 150 degrees geometry to two Ca and two Si atoms. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ca, and two Si atoms. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, one Al, and one Si atom. In the tenth O site, O is bonded to one Ca, two Fe, and one Si atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing OCaFe₂Si trigonal pyramids. In the eleventh O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Ca, one Fe, one Al, and one Si atom.
